To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a strong electron-withdrawal derivatization GC/ECNI method was developed to identify the metabolic pathways of OH-PBDES in rat liver microsome incubation systems.

we developed a novel methodological approach for identification of OH-PDE metabolites and found that the hydroxylation of PBDEs occurs mainly at the ortho- and para-positions on the same brominated phenyl rings, where the first OH-group is present.

the metabolic pathways of the BDE-47 in rat liver microsome (RLM) incubation systems were investigated by the development of a strong electron-withdrawal pentafluorbenzoyl (PFB) derivatization GC/ECNI-MS, and that the second hydroxyation took place on the bromophenyl rings where the first hydroxylation was located.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel GC/ECNI method for the identification and quantification of OH-PBDES and/or BPs in biological matrices and its application to the elucidation of the metabolic pathways in the biota.
the development of a strong electron-withdrawal pentafluoropropionyl derivatization GC/ECNI-MS method and its application in the identification of the metabolic pathways for BDE-47.
the development of a strong electron-withdrawal derivatization technique for the analysis of OH-PBDES and BPs metabolites and the evaluation of their metabolic pathways.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BDE-47 was hydroxylated on the 3- and/or 6-bromophenyl rings, and further hydroxylated at the 2'-position, and the 2',4',6'-tri-OH-BDEs were further hydroxylating at the 2-position.

the hydroxylation of PBDEs takes place on the bromophenyl rings and the hydroxyl group is located on the para position of the bromophenol moiety, and the second hydroxy group is located on another bromophenyl moiety, which is the same as that of the first hydroxide.
the hydroxylation of BDE-28, -47, and -99 takes place on the same ring, where the original bromine is present, and that the second hydroxy group is further introduced on the same ring.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabolic pathways of the PBDEs are not only the hydroxylation of bromophenyl rings but also the formation of dihydroxyl-BDEs and dihydroxyl-dioxins.

the strong electron-withdrawal property of pentafluorophenyl esterification on OH-PBDES/BPs makes cleavage on ECNI easier and results in higher abundance of structure-informative fragment ions in the m/z region of 200-400, facilitating their identification and subsequent quantification by isotope dilution GC/ECNI-MS.

the metabolic pathways of the PBDEs in vivo and in vitro are not only the hydroxylation but also the dihydroxylation, and that the second hydroxy group is located on the same bromo ring where the first one is located.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the PFBoyl derivatisation method developed here can be applied to other PBDEs and/or other environmental contaminants with a phenyl structure, which are known to undergo hydroxylation and bromophenol formation in biological systems.
PFBoyl derivitization is a useful tool for the structural elucidation and quantification of PBDEs metabolites, especially for those with a high number of bromine atoms.
the PFBoyl derivativization GC/ECNI-MS method is a powerful tool for identifying the metabolic pathway of PBDEs.
